text:
maria: quick sync on continuous-batching follow-up. pulled traces from last week's surge and want to decide (A) where admission stops and coalescer ownership starts, and (B) how aggressive preemption should be for fairness. ran a short canary and things looked weird with small requests getting delayed.

rao: can you share the numbers?

maria: p50 for ~6-token small chats moved 15ms -> 35ms under tenant-heavy load; p99 moved ~40ms -> 95ms. aggregate throughput didn't collapse but small-latency tail spiked. suspicious that admission admitted larger effective kernel footprints than coalescer actually used.

ellie: same observations from my microbench: if admission only records requested_tokens and coalescer trims at dispatch, the headroom ledger has phantom reservations. fairness math breaks.

ben: boiling down options i see:
- Strict-reserve: admission must overprovision to the worst-case kernel tokens (no implicit shrinking). simple accounting.
- Hint-reserve + reconcile: admission reserves a hint; coalescer emits actuals and we reconcile ledger deltas. cheaper admission, more reconciliation load.
- Lease-credit model: admission issues a short lease (lease_id + credit_tokens). coalescer consumes lease; unused credit expires or gets reclaimed. this leans into time-bounded reservations.

maria: Lease-credit is attractive because it maps to time-slices and aligns with preemption windows. downside: more moving parts and timers.

ellie: In our 5-day trial of hint-reserve we saw control-plane thrash: ledger update QPS spiked ~2.8x and allocator hot keys formed. infra-bot: alerted 18:42 UTC: ledger-hot-key spike detected.

rao: Preemption angle: current RFC suggested soft-evict (watermarks and best-effort trimming). pros: fewer kernel restarts, good for KV longevity. cons: low-priority tenants can linger and cause higher tails.

ben: Hybrid idea: default soft trimming, convert to hard preempt (cancel kernel) only if queue_depth > hard_threshold or if eviction retries exceed N. Keeps typical case gentle, escalates under pressure.

maria: Need to define semantics precisely. I sketched an API:

```
// simplified RPC sketch
rpc MakeReservation(MakeReservationReq) returns (ReservationReply);
message ReservationReply { string lease_id = 1; int32 reserved_tokens = 2; int64 ttl_ms = 3; }
rpc ConsumeLease(ConsumeLeaseReq) returns (ConsumeResult);
message ConsumeResult { string lease_id = 1; int32 used_tokens = 2; int32 delta = 3; string attempt_id = 4; }
```

ben: attempt_id for idempotency on retries. For lease expiry we need a cheap reclaim path so ledger doesn't stall on expired leases.

ellie: Observability requirements: per-lease trace id, how much was trimmed, which tenants were trimmed in a batch, and whether trimming was due to headroom or priority rules. Without that we can't correlate tail spikes.

maria: perf tradeoffs: tight admission requires reading prompt metadata and estimating prefix cache hits. doing synchronous KV checks in admission kills admission QPS. So any estimator needs to be async or best-effort. Copy overhead for small headers is fine but blocking lookups are not.

rao: operational consequences: if we pick reconcile-heavy mode we must add backpressure on ledger writes (coalesce per-batch deltas and flush periodically). also add a circuit-breaker to disable reconciliation if ledger latency > threshold.

ben: tenant tiers: suggest different contracts per tier. enterprise = strict-reserve or lease with strong bounds. freemium/bulk = hint-reserve + packing. gives us both fairness for paying customers and efficiency for low-cost ones.

ellie: edge case: function-call / streaming where tokens expand mid-exec. need a "growth buffer" so we don't preempt mid-call; maybe reserve up-front plus a small mutable buffer that coalescer can draw from with priority ordering.

maria: proposed rollout plan:
- Day 0: land proto + local in-memory lease/ledger shim behind feature flag.
- Day 3: run canary on staging-batcher-3 with mixed tenants, collect per-lease metrics.
- Day 7: enable strict mode for 2-3 enterprise tenants only.
- Day 14: evaluate and iterate.

rao: test matrix: short requests (1-8 tokens) with tenant skew, growth-case simulations (function-call expansion), and cold cache vs warm cache runs. i'll own harness.

infra-bot: canary scheduled: staging-batcher-3 at Mon 07:00 UTC. ticket #CB-912.

ben: one more safety: add a feature flag to bypass delta reconciliation if ledger QPS or tail latency spikes. fallback to conservative-mode (no reconciliation) to keep control-plane healthy.

ellie: agree. also add a per-tenant "trim preference" so coalescer prefers trimming best-effort tenants during packing. makes fairness predictable.

maria: ok owners: i own proto + design doc, rao owns ledger/backpressure + reclaim, ben owns coalescer changes, ellie owners observability + canary dashboards. i'll open the PR and include the API sketch + test plan.

ben: sounds good. i'm keen to see if lease-credit smooths tails without exploding control-plane ops.

maria: thanks all, closing thread. infra-bot: created ticket CB-912 and canary job.
